title: The river in Shiva's hair
hookLine: a river caught in the dancer's hair: why the Ganga is holy, and why water is poured on Shiva
carry: ganga came down through shiva to free souls
tomorrow: what's behind the curtain at Chidambaram?

lines: THE HAIR FLIES OUT LIKE SPOKES.
cards: Get close to a Nataraja bronze and look at the hair. It doesn't hang down. It flies out to both sides in long locks, like the spokes of a wheel, as if he's spinning so fast the hair can't keep up.
And tangled in them on one side is something tiny: a little woman, half of her shaped like flowing water, her hands folded. That's the river Ganga.

teach.b: Why is a river in his hair? The Ramayana tells it. Long ago, the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara were burned to ash by the anger of a sage, Kapila, and their souls had no rest.

Only the heavenly Ganga, flowing over their ashes, could free them. Two generations tried to bring her down, and failed. Then Bhagiratha practiced austerities so long and so hard that the gods agreed.
But a river falling from heaven would break the earth.

teach.h: SHIVA CATCHES HER IN HIS HAIR.
teach.b: So Bhagiratha turned to Shiva, and Shiva stood beneath the falling river and took her on his head. She vanished into his matted locks, gentled, until he let her out in streams.

teach.h: WHY ASHES GO TO THE GANGA.
teach.b: Bhagiratha led her across the land to the ashes, and his ancestors were set free. That's why the Ganga is the holiest river in Hindu life. Families carry the ashes of their dead to her, hoping for the same release.
Homes keep a small sealed pot of Ganga water for prayers, and for the dying.

teach.h: WHY WATER IS POURED ON SHIVA.
teach.b: And in Shiva temples, water is poured over the linga again and again; many devotees say it recalls this moment, the river landing on his head.
Even the word stuck: in many Indian languages, a huge, patient effort is still called a Bhagiratha effort.

teach.h: SHE CAME DOWN TO SET SOULS FREE.
teach.b: So when a family in New Jersey flies an urn to Haridwar, or a grandmother keeps that little pot on her shelf, they're stepping into Bhagiratha's story: doing the long work for those who came before.
And the wildest part of the dancer, his flying hair, is holding that river with care.

how: In Nataraja bronzes the locks fly out toward the encircling ring of flames, with the small figure of Ganga among them; Hindus keep Ganga water at home for worship and for the dying, immerse the ashes of the dead in the Ganga, and pour water over the Shiva linga in abhisheka.

o: a king who prays to bring rain down to his fields
the river Ganga, caught in Shiva's hair so she could free souls
a river goddess who dances inside a ring of fire

games.q: the hair and the ring — tap the pairs.
p: brought the Ganga down to earth
the tiny figure in the hair
holy water kept at home for prayer

s: in the Ramayana, the Ganga came down to free the souls of Bhagiratha's ancestors
her water over the ashes of Sagara's sons set them free. families still bring ashes to her.
the small figure in his hair is the river Ganga
caught when she fell from heaven, and let out gently.
Shiva caught the Ganga to keep her from ever reaching the earth
he caught her so her fall wouldn't break the earth, then let her flow on.

games.q: you're Bhagiratha. the gods have agreed to send the Ganga down, but a river falling from heaven would break the earth. what do you do?
o: ask the gods to send only a little water.
turn to Shiva to catch her.
dig a great basin to hold her.
games.why: Shiva stands under the falling river and takes her into his locks, where she's slowed and gentled before she flows across the land.

practice: If you can, fill a small cup of water. Pour it slowly, in a thin stream, the way water is poured over Shiva in a temple: over a plant, or into your other palm.

If you pray, say Om Namah Shivaya with the stream, or offer it to God in your own words. If you don't, think of someone who came before you, and of the long effort it took to get you here. Let the stream run until the cup is empty.

wordCard.voice: The Ganga, the river in Shiva's hair: she came down from heaven to set souls free, and he made her gentle enough to reach the earth.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Ganga, the river goddess caught in the locks of Shiva's hair.

carryVoice: Your line: Ganga came down through Shiva to free souls. That's why her water is holy. Same time tomorrow.
